learning_outcomes.text: Knows basic concepts, classification of power grids, grid structure, grid systems and their properties.
Knows the principles of modeling elements and complex network systems for calculations in steady states (power flows).
The student knows the construction of electrical devices used in the generation, transmission, distribution and use of electrical energy.
The student knows the threats to which electrical devices and switchgears are subjected.
The student is able to calculate characteristic electrical quantities determining the selection of electrical devices and apparatus under normal operating conditions and during fault states.
Is able to perform calculations of power flows, voltage drops and power losses in open networks.

syllabus_topics: Estimation of loads in a distribution network
Integration of distributed sources in a distribution power network
Analysis of the voltage profile of an active network
Optimization of voltage regulation in a distribution network
Frequency regulation in interconnected power systems
Reliability analysis of selected distribution network structures
Analysis of short-circuit conditions in a distribution network

Design of a low-voltage network supplying a residential area consisting of multi-family and single-family housing and public utility facilities. Estimation of power demand, design of the supply network and selection of its elements.
Introduction to power grids issues.
Contemporary conditions related to the operation of the power system.
Modern technologies in the documentation of network infrastructure facilities.
Basics of network modeling.
Steady-state analysis.
Calculation tools.
State estimation.
Selected issues related to the reliability of power grids.
Active power balancing and frequency regulation in power systems.
Power and electrical energy losses in networks.
Methods of loss analysis.
Reduction of power and energy losses in power grids.
Methodology and means of voltage regulation in power grids.
Specificity of regulatory issues in transmission and distribution networks.
Electrical devices in the power system.
Basic concepts.
Exposures and operating conditions of power devices.
Reliability of supply.
General division and functions of electrical apparatus, switchgears and distribution boards.
Division of circuit breakers and their basic parameters, constructions of circuit breakers and selection criteria at various voltage levels.
Construction of disconnectors, switch-disconnectors, earthing switches, insulating switch-disconnectors and contactors.
Selection principles.
Current and voltage transformers: general division, scope of applications and characteristic parameters.
Power stations.
Low and medium voltage power switchgears.
assessment_rules: The overall assessment for the course is based on an examination for lectures, tests or projects for auditorium classes, and tests or projects for project classes. Student preparation for auditorium classes may be assessed through oral statements or written colloquiums. Project classes are evaluated based on the method of project execution and the final result.
